title: Cohomology comparison through a vanishing bound
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category small in a universe containing the sites and coefficients [def-weil-size-convention], endowed with two site structures $\tau$ and $\tau'$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] such that every $\tau'$-covering is a $\tau$-covering. For $X\in\mathcal C$, let $\mathcal C_\tau/X$ and $\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X$ be the slice sites: their objects are arrows $U\to X$, their morphisms are commutative triangles, and their coverings are those whose underlying families cover $U$ in the respective topology. Let $\epsilon_X:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] with direct image the identity on underlying presheaves and inverse image $\tau$ sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For $f:X\to Y$ write $f_{\tau'}$ for the relocalization morphism of slice topoi whose inverse image sends $H$ to $(U\to X)\mapsto H(U\to X\to Y)$. Higher direct images below mean the ordinary right derived functors on abelian sheaves, computed using injective resolutions. Suppose that a class $\mathcal P$ of morphisms and full subcategories $\mathcal A'_X\subset\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ have the following properties. Each $\mathcal A'_X$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and extensions (the weak Serre condition). Assume in addition:

(1) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$ and any $Y'\to Y$, the fibre product $X\times_Y Y'$ exists and $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ lies in $\mathcal P$.

(2) For every $f:X\to Y$, one has $f_{\tau'}^{-1}(\mathcal A'_Y)\subset\mathcal A'_X$.

(3) Every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ already satisfies the $\tau$ sheaf condition on $\mathcal C/X$.

(4) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$, $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ and every $i\geq0$, one has $R^if_{\tau',*}H'\in\mathcal A'_Y$.

For each $X$, let $\mathcal A_X$ be the full subcategory of $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)$ consisting of sheaves isomorphic to $\epsilon_X^{-1}H'$ with $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$. For $r\geq0$, let $(V_r)$ mean that $R^i\epsilon_{X,*}H=0$ for all $X$, $H\in\mathcal A_X$ and $1\leq i\leq r$. Assume $(V_r)$. Let $L\in D^+(\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $\mathcal H^i(L)=0$ for $i<0$ and $\mathcal H^i(L)\in\mathcal A'_X$ for $0\leq i\leq r$ (cohomology sheaves for the standard t-structure [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category]). The canonical pullback, defined by the derived adjunction unit and the identification of derived sections after derived direct image, is an isomorphism
$$H^r_{\tau'}(X,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r_\tau(X,\epsilon_X^{-1}L).$$
Here hypercohomology is $H^r$ of the complex of sections of a bounded-below injective resolution. This isomorphism is natural in $L$.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, lemma-V-implies-cohomology-general; naturality/canonical maps are those of its proof and section-compare-general.

proof.text: Fix $X$ and write $F=\epsilon_X^{-1}$ and $G=\epsilon_{X,*}$. Abelian sheaves on either small slice site form a Grothendieck abelian category: apply [lem-cbc-sieve-module-sheaves-grothendieck] with $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, identifying an abelian group with its unique unital $\mathbf Z$-module structure. The functor $F$ is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], and its termwise action commutes with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. For $A'\in\mathcal A'_X$, assumption (3) says that $A'$ is already a $\tau$-sheaf. Its sheafification unit $A'\to GFA'$ is therefore an isomorphism: its inverse is the unique map extending the identity of $A'$, and uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] makes both composites identities. Also $FA'\in\mathcal A_X$ by definition.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, the equality epsilon_* epsilon^{-1} H^q(L)=H^q(L); Tag 0EZ3, assumption (3).

proof.text: Use the canonical derived unit $u_M:M\to RGF M$ for $F\dashv RG$. This is the ringed-topos adjunction for $\epsilon_X$ with constant integer coefficient sheaves; module inverse image is the exact abelian inverse image $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor], its derived inverse image is the termwise functor. The unit commutes with every integer shift by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-adjunction-shift]. The identity functor and $RGF$ are triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-triangle-morphism] makes the units into a morphism between each distinguished triangle and its $RGF$ image, including the connecting arrow. This records the particular canonical maps that the argument will compare.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, the canonical map L -> R epsilon_* epsilon^{-1} L; Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), with constant Z coefficients.

proof.text: For $A'\in\mathcal A'_X$ in degree zero, [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification] identifies $\mathcal H^p(RGF(A'[0]))$ with $R^pG(FA')$ for $p\geq0$. In degree zero the map of $u_{A'[0]}$ is the underived unit of Step 1: for an injective resolution $FA'\to I$, its representative is $A'\to GFA'\to GI$, and $G$ preserves kernels as a right adjoint. Here $R^0G=G$ by [lem-sp-derived-well-defined]. For $1\leq p\leq r$ the target is zero by $(V_r)$; the source is zero as well. Both sides vanish in negative degrees by [lem-sp-shift-identification], part (3). Hence $u_{A'[0]}$ is an isomorphism on cohomology in every degree $\leq r$. For $0\leq q\leq r$, shift compatibility from Step 2 and [lem-sp-shift-identification] give the same conclusion for $u_{A'[-q]}$: its degree-$i$ map is the degree-$(i-q)$ map before shifting, and $i-q\leq r$ whenever $i\leq r$.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, vanishing of R^p epsilon_* epsilon^{-1} H^q(L) for 0<p<=r; derived.tex Tags 015A and 05TH.

proof.text: Put $K=\tau_{\leq r}L$ and let $c:K\to L$ be the canonical inclusion. Then $K$ has cohomology only in $[0,r]$, with $\mathcal H^q(K)=\mathcal H^q(L)\in\mathcal A'_X$ there. The map $c$ is an isomorphism on cohomology through degree $r$ and is a monomorphism in degree $r+1$, since its source in that degree is zero. Exactness of $F$ gives the same assertions for $Fc:FK\to FL$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso], with $n=r$ and the global-sections functor on each slice site. Its Grothendieck hypotheses hold by Step 1. We obtain isomorphisms $H^r_{\tau'}(X,K)\to H^r_{\tau'}(X,L)$ and $H^r_\tau(X,FK)\to H^r_\tau(X,FL)$. It therefore suffices to prove the canonical comparison for $K$, and then use naturality with respect to $c$.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, the omitted detail, first truncate at r; derived.tex Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing), part (2).

proof.text: Write $K_q=\tau_{\leq q}K$ for $-1\leq q\leq r$ and $B_q=\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]$ for $0\leq q\leq r$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] there are distinguished triangles $K_{q-1}\to K_q\to B_q\to K_{q-1}[1]$. We prove by induction on $q$ that $\mathcal H^i(u_{K_q})$ is an isomorphism for all $i\leq r$. The base $K_{-1}=0$ holds because $K$ is connective and additive functors send zero to zero. Step 3 applies to every $B_q$. The units give morphisms of these triangles by Step 2; their long exact cohomology sequences are natural by [lem-sp-long-exact-of-triangle], with cohomology homological by [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact].

source.place: Tag 0EZB, “small detail omitted”, written with the finite truncation filtration underlying its spectral sequence; derived.tex Tag 08J5.

proof.text:
For the induction step, fix $0\leq q\leq r$ and $i\leq r$ and compare the exact five-term segments
$$\mathcal H^{i-1}(B_q)\to\mathcal H^i(K_{q-1})\to\mathcal H^i(K_q)\to\mathcal H^i(B_q)\to\mathcal H^{i+1}(K_{q-1})$$
and their $RGF$ counterparts. The first, second and fourth vertical maps are isomorphisms by Step 3 and the induction hypothesis. The fifth is an isomorphism if $i<r$. If $i=r$, it is still a monomorphism: $K_{q-1}$ has no cohomology in degree $r+1$ since $q-1\leq r-1$, so its source is zero. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] therefore hold, giving the required middle isomorphism. This proves the induction. Since $K_r=K$, the actual unit $u_K$ induces isomorphisms in degrees $\leq r$. Also $\mathcal H^{r+1}(u_K)$ is a monomorphism because $\mathcal H^{r+1}(K)=0$. This last observation is essential when applying derived sections.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, “small detail omitted”; homology.tex Tag 05QB (lemma-five-lemma), applied to the canonical unit on truncation triangles.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso] once more, now to $u_K:K\to RGF K$ and $v=\Gamma(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X,-)$, with $n=r$. The bounded-below hypothesis holds for $RGF K$ because it is a right derived functor on $D^+$; the Grothendieck hypotheses hold by Step 1, and Step 6 verifies both the isomorphism range and the degree-$(r+1)$ monomorphism. Consequently the specific map $H^r(R\Gamma_{\tau'}(u_K))$ is an isomorphism. This argument does not assume that an arbitrary morphism which is an isomorphism only through degree $r$ remains so after derived sections.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, passage from the derived unit to hypercohomology; derived.tex Tag 05TC, applied with the additional monomorphism checked in Step 6.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $\epsilon_X$ followed by the structure morphism of the $\tau'$ slice topos to the punctual topos, all with constant $\mathbf Z$ coefficients. Ordinary sections satisfy $\Gamma_{\tau'}G=\Gamma_\tau$ because $G$ leaves underlying presheaves unchanged. The cited canonical composition isomorphism therefore identifies $R\Gamma_{\tau'}RGFK$ with $R\Gamma_\tau FK$, naturally in $K$. Composing this isomorphism with Step 7 gives
$$H^r_{\tau'}(X,K)\xrightarrow{H^r(R\Gamma_{\tau'}u_K)}H^r(R\Gamma_{\tau'}RGFK)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^r_\tau(X,FK).$$
This is precisely the comparison specified in the statement, since it is the derived adjunction unit followed by the canonical derived-sections/direct-image identification.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, first line, using Tag 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded); composition Tag 0D6E.

proof.text: The derived unit and the composition isomorphism in Step 8 are natural transformations. Applied to $c:K\to L$, their naturality makes a commutative square with the comparison for $K$ above, the comparison for $L$ below, and the two vertical isomorphisms of Step 4. Hence the comparison for $L$ is an isomorphism. For any morphism $L\to L'$ between complexes satisfying the hypotheses, the same naturality square proves naturality of the resulting isomorphism; no choices of resolutions or truncation isomorphisms alter the canonical map. This includes $r=0$, where $(V_0)$ is empty and the induction has only $q=0$. Assumptions (1), (2), (4) and weak Serre closure remain part of the comparison situation but are not needed beyond the supplied vanishing and assumption (3) for this lemma.

source.place: Tag 0EZB, conclusion; naturality of the derived unit and of Tag 0D6E.
